practical.title: Analyze and Implement Linear Search for Strings
practical.sourceActivity: Analyze and Implement Linear Search for Strings

files.description: Runnable C starter file for the practical.

tasks.title: Scene 1 — Observe & Understand: Run a baseline linear search for strings
tasks.narratorGuide: Hello! First we'll run a baseline program that searches a small array of names for two targets: one that exists ("Charlie") and one that doesn't ("Frank"). Focus on where strcmp is called — that's the comparison that determines equality of two C strings. Running the program shows concrete output you can verify. Understanding this working baseline helps when we later change only one or two lines to alter behavior (for example, making comparisons case-insensitive). Observing the current output also sets measurable expectations for later verification steps.

tasks.title: Scene 2 — Modify & Experiment: Make comparisons case-insensitive (1-2 line change)
tasks.narratorGuide: Great — in this scene you'll change the comparison to be case-insensitive. This is a small, safe change with big consequences: it broadens matching for user input. Replace strcmp with strcasecmp (or implement equivalent tolower-based logic if strcasecmp isn't available). Then compile and run. Observe that "charlie" now matches "Charlie". This exercise shows how tiny changes at the comparison point affect program behavior and user experience.

tasks.title: Scene 3 — Build & Integrate: Report all matches and count comparisons (instrumentation)
tasks.narratorGuide: Now instrument the search. Instead of stopping at the first match, collect every matching index into an array and count how many strcmp calls you perform. This teaches an important point: even if you find a match early, if your algorithm must find all matches you'll still inspect remaining elements. Run the program to see three cases: duplicates, first-element match, and not-found. Record the comparisons printed — these are direct empirical measures of cost and map to Big O reasoning.

tasks.title: Scene 4 — Verify & Extend: Edge cases and prefix matching (extension)
tasks.narratorGuide: In this final scene we verify edge cases and extend the search to prefix matching using strncmp. This demonstrates how small API changes let you support new requirements (e.g., searching by prefix). Also run the long-string test: although we only check a short prefix, in general longer strings increase per-compare cost. Finally, reflect on the three analysis questions: best-case, worst-case, and how string length affects complexity.

safety.learnerWarning: This practical runs in an isolated workspace. Do not use real credentials or production resources.

cleanup.instructions: Discard the isolated workspace after completion.
